title: Fix private upgrade window triggering batcher state corruption under mixed-length workloads
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Customer (FinReg Inc.) reported periodic latency spikes and failed responses from Private deployments after platform upgrades. Root cause traced to a narrow upgrade-time window where a background state-migration touched batcher admission counters and KV-prefetch state concurrently, causing inconsistent admission accounting and eventual batcher state corruption under mixed-length workloads (short requests + long-context generations). The corruption manifests as sustained small-request suppression and long-context tail latency increases. This ticket coordinates a customer-facing hotfix, regression tests, and a rollout strategy across Hosted/Dedicated/Private channels.
reproduction_steps: 1) Stand up a Private runtime (v1.18-stable) with mixed tenant config: 60% short-gen traffic (<=64 tokens) and 40% long-gen traffic (>=4096 tokens) generated by synthetic loaddriver.
2) Schedule an in-place control-plane upgrade that triggers the state-migration (upgrade binary v1.18->v1.19-canary with migration flag enabled).

3) Observe admission counters: run 'redwoodctl inspect batcher --tenant T1 --metrics' and capture pre/post-upgrade values; look for negative/low available_admit tokens and K/V prefetch version mismatch logs.
4) Confirm symptoms: sustained 3-5x p99 on short requests and queued long-context batches that never complete (deadtime), manifesting as 504s to the client on heavy mixed workload.
5) Reproduce locally with a controlled time-window by pausing the migration at migration-step-2 and concurrently issuing a microburst of short requests to trigger the race.
Notes: Reproduction requires simulating realistic KV hit-rate distributions; a synthetic driver and seed dataset is attached in links.
recent_activity: 2026-03-01: Customer FinReg Inc. opened escalation after seeing multi-hour degradation during scheduled maintenance window (Asha triaged).
2026-03-02: Initial triage — telemetry points to admission counter reset around migration commit; hypothesized race between migration finalizer and batcher eviction thread (Lucas assigned).
2026-03-03: Reproduced in private staging using test harness (alpha), captured core dumps and admission counter deltas; created minimal repro harness in repo (link in PRs).
2026-03-05: Implemented a guarded-migration patch that takes a lightweight lock around admission counter update and KV-prefetch version bump; ran unit tests and basic load tests (PR #7842).

2026-03-07: Observed fix prevents immediate corruption but introduced small latency bump for long-gen median under synthetic load; reverted and iterated to reduce locking window (branch: fix/guarded-migration-optim).
2026-03-09: Security review passed for private-only migration guard; added feature-flag to toggle behavior for Hosted and Dedicated while we expand test coverage.

2026-03-11: Canary rollout to FinReg staging succeeded (30% traffic for 4 hours); telemetry shows p99 short requests returned to baseline and KV prefetch hit-rate stable. Preparing customer patch release and a wider canary for Dedicated clusters.
2026-03-12: Drafted post-deploy verification playbook for on-call and SRE; scheduling coordinated Dedicated rollout on 2026-03-15 and Hosted patch on 2026-03-16 during low-traffic windows.
rollback_plan: If rollback required on any environment: 1) revert runtime binary to v1.18-stable and re-run migration rollback hook (ensured idempotent), 2) disable feature-flag and restart batcher processes gracefully, 3) open immediate incident bridge and escalate to SRE and release leads. Confirm traffic thresholds before returning to normal operations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary in FinReg staging (30%) shows short-request p99 within 10% of baseline for 6 hours.
2) No admission counter inconsistencies observed in logs for 48 hours post-upgrade across Private and Dedicated canaries.
3) Unit + integration tests added to repro race and included in CI (green on main branch).
4) Post-deploy verification playbook validated with on-call and SRE runbook sign-off.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add a migration-safety gate to the control plane that prevents concurrent admission writes without transaction semantics.
2) Expand chaos tests to include staged migration window scenarios (simulate control-plane delays + microbursts).
3) Ship improved observability: explicit admission counter delta metrics, migration-step markers, and an alert when admission counter goes negative or changes >50% in 5s.
4) Update upgrade docs for Private deployments to include recommended maintenance window and required preflight KV consistency check.
